name: Stevin’s hydrostatic pressure analysis
description: Equilibrium analysis of fluid pressure and vessel shape.

impact.note: Extended Archimedean hydrostatics to pressure on vessel walls and bottoms; known to a specialist readership, with Pascal and a few others following.

date.basis: Year of the source-bounded episode, not necessarily invention.

events.statement: Stevin’s 1586 Waterwichts discussed equilibrium and the equal base loading of differently shaped vessels with equal base area and liquid height.

evidence.supports: Cambridge explains the equal-base-area and height conditions.
Dutch text guide identifies base pressure and the paradox.

contributions.resource: Developed or authored the described account.

evidence.supports: Cambridge explains the equal-base-area and height conditions.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated source-bounded episode in this record, not a claim of worldwide priority.

caveats: The equal-load comparison assumes the relevant fluid and equal heights and base areas; it is not a claim that all fluid forces are independent of vessel geometry. Stevin built on earlier hydrostatics.

research.note: Chronology distinguishes composition or formulation from later surviving textual witnesses. Independent review checked the event dating and scope against the cited work, historical source, edition metadata or modern translation, as applicable. The quoted Dutch preface and Cambridge historical account support the Archimedes connection.

links.statement: Stevin explicitly discussed Archimedes’ On Floating Bodies and extended its hydrostatics with analyses of force at vessel bases and walls.

evidence.supports: Stevin identifies Archimedes’ On Floating Bodies; the guide locates the later propositions.
Cambridge history describes his extension of Archimedean hydrostatics.
